title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No real error. One small point: condition (a) plus 'S contains the vertices of order ≥3' leaves implicit that isolated points and order-2 points may or may not lie in S. Non-compactness of the components of X∖S forces isolated points into S, and order-2 points outside S simply lie inside open edges. The equivalence stated is correct.

ideas.what: Encoding a graph with legs as (vertices S, half-edges Î, involution σ on Î possibly with fixed points, origin map Î→S), with legs = fixed points of σ
ideas.modern_name: Graph in the flag/half-edge formalism (Kontsevich–Manin, Getzler–Kapranov, Behrend–Manin stable graphs), legs as σ-fixed flags
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich–Manin (1994), Getzler–Kapranov 'Modular operads' (1998); half-edge with involution formalism for ordinary graphs going back to Serre 'Arbres, amalgames, SL2' (1977)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme in this form as far as I know; Grothendieck's dessins/cartes formalism there uses permutation triples instead

ideas.what: Topological realisation: compact X with finite S, star near S, components of X∖S non-compact 1-manifolds with boundary; equivalently a 1-complex with S ⊇ {vertices of order ≥3} and S → π_0(X) surjective
ideas.modern_name: Geometric realisation of a graph with open/half-open legs (tails as half-open edges)

ideas.what: Use of these graphs with legs and genus labels (ν-graphs) to index the stratification 'at infinity' of M_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs / dual graphs indexing the boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; systematised by Kontsevich, Getzler–Kapranov, Arbarello–Cornalba
ideas.where_published: Hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{g,ν} at infinity), but not with this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the now-standard half-edge-with-involution formalism in which legs are the fixed points of the involution. He gives it explicitly as a topological classification of 1-complexes with free ends, to index the boundary structure of M_{g,ν}. If these notes date from the early-to-mid 1980s, this predates the usual attribution of the formalism (Kontsevich–Manin 1994, Getzler–Kapranov 1998).
missed.quote: On n'exige plus que σ soit sans pts fixes — l'ens des pts fixes, I, correspond aux "bandes aplaties" (next page); 'Ceci se classifie combinatoirement par des systèmes (S, Î, σ_Î, o_Î)'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority note for the stable-graph/modular-operad formalism. It is mathematically routine and largely folklore, so its significance is attribution only.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a clean, correct formulation of what later became the standard stable-graph (flags with involution, legs as fixed points) formalism, plus its topological model. It is interesting as an early independent appearance tied to M_{g,ν} at infinity, but the idea is simple and folklore-level, so specialists would not be very surprised.
